note: Source manifest for the ORCH-753 gold cohort. The paper text is NOT committed; it lives at C:/t/eval-fulltext/<PMCID>.txt and gold.load_fulltext refuses a text whose sha256 differs.
citation: Sato T et al. A non-carboxylating pentose bisphosphate pathway in halophilic archaea Communications biology 2022.
pathway_in_one_line: A newly identified haloarchaeal nucleoside degradation route that converts the ribose moiety of guanosine to dihydroxyacetone phosphate and ethylene glycol without any carboxylation step.
scope_note: In scope: guanosine + phosphate -> ribose-1-phosphate + guanine (guanosine phosphorylase), R1P + ATP -> ribose-1,5-bisphosphate (ATP-dependent R1P kinase), R15P -> ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate (R15P isomerase), RuBP -> ribulose-1-phosphate (the previously unknown RuBP phosphatase), Ru1P -> DHAP + glycolaldehyde (Ru1P aldolase), and glycolaldehyde + NADH -> ethylene glycol. Adjacent and explicitly contrasted: the Thermococcus kodakarensis route where RuBP is carboxylated to 3-phosphoglycerate by Rubisco, the non-oxidative pentose phosphate pathway, the ribulose monophosphate pathway, and the R5P -> R1P -> R15P -> PRPP proposal from other work. Assay-reporter reactions (pyruvate kinase, lactate dehydrogenase, glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenase coupling) are off-pathway.
selected_because: A whole novel pathway established enzyme by enzyme, every intermediate named in words, in a domain of life the gold has never seen. The deliberate contrast with the carboxylating Rubisco route gives a built-in near-miss test: a correct extraction must keep RuBP -> Ru1P and must not substitute RuBP -> 3-PGA.
